A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 18 readable pages, Figures 1–5, and Appendices A–E. Text, equations and visual inspection support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original sampling simulations on Gaussian mixtures and higher-dimensional Gaussian distributions, including bias and mixing-speed results in Figures 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original sampling simulations and their reported bias and mixing-speed results in Section 4 and Figures 1–5.

M1.justification: The noise-corrected update in Equations (6)–(8) and half-denoising specialization in Equations (14)–(16) are unchanged. The added final-correction perspective in Section 3.2.1 explains the existing sampler rather than revising its specified procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate two-dimensional Gaussian mixtures with one to four components, Gaussian distributions in dimensions 5, 10 and 100, and the same two-component mixing scenario. Noise-level coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain Basic Langevin, Oracle Langevin, their quarter-step variants where evaluated, and exact-sampling references. The added citation discussing walk-jump comparisons does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same step-size rules, 1,000,000-step simulations, final-30% analysis, density-estimation settings and distance metrics. The initialization and 100-step design of the mixing experiment are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The step-size controls, noise-level comparisons, density visualizations and mixing-speed analysis are retained with identical evidence. No ablation, robustness test or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains standard-error bars, and Figure 5 retains averaging over 10,000 runs. Repeated-run and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–5 contain identical plot content, and the experimental findings are unchanged. Both versions report performance close to Oracle Langevin at matched step sizes and no apparent mixing-speed loss from noise correction.

T1.justification: The theorem statements, assumptions, equations and Appendix A–E proofs are unchanged. The added discussion acknowledges limitations and cites further analysis without supplying a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: correcting noisy-score bias using one noise level and obtaining half-denoising as a special case. The abstract's wording adjustment does not change their scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.2.1 adds an interpretation involving ordinary noisy-score Langevin sampling followed by a final correction. Section 3.2.2 explicitly emphasizes the serious limitation that Theorem 2 concerns one step starting from the target distribution.

D1.justification: Implementation and simulation details are retained, with no new code/data access information or computational-resource disclosure. The added author email is a contact-header edit rather than technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Beyler and Bach (2025), citing its analysis inspired by this paper's earlier preprint and its comparison with walk-jump sampling. This is a limited addition to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds two short discussion paragraphs and a related-work sentence, adjusts abstract word order, adds an author email and identifies the acknowledged Action Editor. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Text and equation spacing produce modest page reflow and shifted section and appendix starts. Figures 1–5 retain their panels, axes, legends and captions; there is no substantive figure or table redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 more explicitly acknowledges the restricted guarantee of Theorem 2 and adds a useful sampling interpretation and research attribution in Sections 3.2 and 5. These changes modestly improve transparency and context, while the underlying method, proofs and empirical support remain unchanged.
